correctness.rationale: In dimension three, nonpermutability can occur only for two distinct lines, and those lines permute exactly when their unique spanning plane is a Lie subalgebra; this gives the universal count directly. Solvable algebras admit a two-dimensional abelian ideal and their planes are counted by projective eigenlines of a 2-by-2 adjoint action. For perfect algebras, the bracket matrix is invertible and symmetric, and Lie-subalgebra planes are the q+1 projective zeros of the resulting conic/linear-square equation. The factorization-number count is an independent incidence enumeration and specializes to the published Heisenberg/sl2 formula.

originality.rationale: Qualified to the best of our knowledge. The new subalgebra-commutativity paper computes special Heisenberg and sl2 cases but does not state the general plane-count formula or four-value classification. The comaximal-graph paper contains the solvable plane counts, which are treated as prior art, but predates the new invariant. Targeted searches found no matching universal formula, complete finite-field classification, or classification-free perfect-case q+1 theorem.

value.rationale: The result completely determines a newly introduced invariant in dimension three over every finite field, identifies sharp extremizers and all four possible values, explains the published Heisenberg/sl2 coincidence, and links the invariant exactly to lattice size, factorization number, and the line-line edge count of the comaximal graph.

disclaimer: Not independent validation, peer review, formal verification, or a guarantee of first discovery.
